sections.h2: Why selling in Port St. Lucie is different
sections.html:
St. Lucie County's biggest city is also one of its youngest. Estimates put Port St. Lucie at 268,062 people in July 2025, a rise of 30.9 percent over April 2020, and the city expects another 125,000 residents within 10 to 15 years.

All that growth puts new construction near almost every street, and your house competes with it. Buyers can line yours up against a fresh build, so condition and price both count. Most sellers choose one of three routes.

Before choosing, list what you know about the house: roof and air conditioner age, any septic system, open permits, HOA dues and who lives there. A cash buyer discounts for problems, and a retail buyer finds them in an inspection, so being upfront saves time either way.

  • Agent listing: the widest exposure to buyers, along with repair requests.
  • Owner-handled sale: lower cost, with the paperwork on you.
  • Cash offer: a fit for deferred work, a vacancy or a short timeline.

A development group incorporated the city in 1961 to sell quarter-acre lots to retirees, with no sidewalks, streetlights, water or sewer. General Development Corporation turned 66 square miles into mostly single-family lots in the 1960s, and later growth reached St. Lucie West and land west of I-95.

That layout explains why many early lots were sold without sewer service. The city is converting septic systems to sewer in one of the larger projects of its kind, and the city utility can tell you where your street stands. A buyer will ask, and a cash buyer will price in any septic work.

sections.h2: Property taxes and Save Our Homes
sections.html:
The city's cut of a typical bill is just 22 percent; the county, school district, fire district and others share the remainder. Assessments are redone each January 1 by the St. Lucie County Property Appraiser. Your buyer starts without your exemptions and caps, which can raise the bill.

Save Our Homes keeps a homestead's annual rise to the smaller of 3 percent or CPI, and savings begin to build in the second year. File or renew between January 1 and March 1. The homestead stays with you as an owner, not with a new address.

Amendment 3 won approval on November 3, 2026, and a bigger non-school homestead exemption follows in 2027. Ask the St. Lucie office how it affects your parcel.

  • Bills arrive in early November, and the early-payment discount steps down from 4 percent in November to 3, 2 and 1 percent in December, January and February.
  • Anything unpaid is delinquent on April 1.
  • Have the title agent prorate this year's bill at closing.

A court foreclosure ends with a clerk's auction, set under section 45.031 for 20 to 35 days after final judgment unless the plaintiff allows more time. The winning bidder puts down 5 percent. If nobody objects in the 10 days after the certificate of sale, the clerk issues the certificate of title.

Owners of a homestead need to ask the clerk about leftover funds within 10 days of the auction. A private sale that closes first may leave you more equity, so phone a lender or attorney as soon as judgment is entered. Stamp tax on the certificate of title is figured on the highest bid.

Documentary stamp tax on a deed is 70 cents for each $100 of consideration here, with an assumed mortgage included. Because every party is liable, your contract should say who pays, and the clerk takes the tax at recording.

A land conveyance needs two subscribing witnesses under section 689.01, and the witnessing can happen by audio-video link.

  • Ask every lender for a payoff letter.
  • Check city records for open permits on sheds, pools, enclosures or additions.
  • Gather HOA or special-district statements if the neighborhood has them.

In heat and humidity, an inspector looks first at the age of the air conditioning and the roof. A home beside the North Fork of the St. Lucie River or a canal invites flood-zone and insurance questions, so keep your policy and permit records for roof, window and enclosure work handy.

For a house within a short drive of the river, mention trails and parks in your pitch. Buyers compare those amenities with newer neighborhoods farther west.

sections.h2: Selling a vacant or rented house
sections.html:
A vacant house in this climate needs attention. Keep the air conditioning running at a safe setting, have someone check for leaks after storms and keep the yard presentable, since a neglected property invites lowball offers and sometimes code letters from the city.

If tenants live there, the sale does not cancel the lease. The buyer takes the house subject to it, so give the title agent a copy of the lease, the deposit records and the tenant's contact details. A cash buyer who wants the house empty may offer to wait until the lease ends, so ask what the buyer plans before you agree. Put any agreed move-out date in the contract, along with who handles the deposit and the final utility bills.

1. Give the buyer the address, payoff amount and any tenant or vacancy details.
  2. Read each written offer for price, repair terms and closing day.
  3. The title agent searches the record and asks lenders for payoffs.
  4. Sign the deed with two witnesses present.
  5. The clerk records it, and you get your money.

For the first conversation, have a current mortgage statement, your newest tax bill, an HOA contact and the repairs you already know of. That lets a buyer write a firm offer and lets the title agent open the file at once. Put three questions to every buyer: who pays for the title policy, how long the offer is good, and whether an inspection can change the price.

At the table you will sign the deed and the settlement statement, so ask for copies of both. Once the clerk records the deed, your money is released and ownership passes. Give the buyer the keys, garage openers and any gate or community access cards, and end your utilities as of that day.

With no buyer's lender involved, title drives the timeline. Plan on a few days for payoffs, HOA statements and the signing.

faqs.q: Is a cash offer realistic for a Port St. Lucie house?
faqs.a: Yes, and more so when the house needs work or the date is fixed. There is no lender appraisal, though the title must be clear and the deed witnessed and recorded.

faqs.q: Does a buyer inherit my homestead exemption in Port St. Lucie?
faqs.a: No. Your exemptions and caps end with the sale, and the buyer starts at the new assessment.

faqs.q: How long until a foreclosure sale after judgment?
faqs.a: Typically 20 to 35 days under section 45.031. Closing a private sale before then can protect equity.

faqs.q: Who pays documentary stamps on the deed?
faqs.a: The contract assigns it, but each party stays liable under state rules. The rate is 70 cents per $100 in this county.

faqs.q: What share of my tax bill is the city's?
faqs.a: About 22 percent. The county, school district, fire district and other taxing bodies split the rest.
